findings.message: [review/consistency] This actor-exclusion filter contradicts the stated invariant of the phase specs this feature was built against. Spec 1f61f624 (phase 3) constrains: "The notification set is a function of the STATE CHANGE, not of who performed it: exactly TWO notificationService.create calls for SUBMITTED and APPROVED cancellations, exactly ONE for DRAFT" and "Self-notification is not suppressed: when the cancelling actor is the resolved recipient, the notification is still written. The exactly-one rule holds regardless of actor identity." Spec 9244f013 (phase 6) repeats it: "no case may assert suppression on the basis of the actor being the recipient", and its success criterion #3 requires the DRAFT case to assert exactly one notification. [review/test-coverage] This assertion inverts a pre-existing case rather than extending it additively. The phase-6 spec (9244f013) constrains "Additive extension only: every pre-existing test case ... must remain byte-for-byte in intent — no case deleted, renamed, skipped, or weakened", and its success criterion #3 requires "a DRAFT cancellation still produces EXACTLY ONE notification (requester only) — the pre-existing DRAFT assertion is unchanged and no approver notification is added on that path." The pre-existing DRAFT case previously asserted `toHaveLength(1)` with `recipientId === REQUESTER_ID`; it now asserts zero, and the sibling case at line 988 was renamed from "sends exactly one cancellation notification for the original" to "notifies only the requester when the canceller IS the recorded approver". Both copies are added by this PR's diff. The duplicated block also swallows the blank line before it, so the second copy's heading is glued to the previous bullet. A reader (and the context/drift agents that consume this file) now sees two conflicting-looking records of the same phase.

  Fix: Delete the second copy (lines 1774–1785) and keep the first (1762–1773); they are byte-identical, so no content is lost.

[review/architecture] This branch's `agents.yaml` reverts the consult completion cap that `origin/main` established. Verified with `git show origin/main:agents.yaml`: main sets `max_tokens: 32000` for all five consultable agents (domain-architect-agent, data-architect-agent, app-architect-agent, chief-architect-agent, planner-agent), with the rationale recorded in main's own comments ("1.11x HEADROOM IS NOT HEADROOM … 32,000 is 1.48x the pooled maximum"; "`data-architect-agent` was TRUNCATING at 0.66x"). On this branch those five are 6000 / 6000 / 6000 / 12000 / 24000 — i.e. the branch reintroduces the exact cap main documented as truncating. Because the merge is a squash, merging this branch silently undoes that decision. The same class of staleness applies to `review-agent`'s `token_budget: 1600000` (main: 1200000) and to `docs/DECISIONS.md`, where main's "🔴 RESTORED 2026-10-11" provenance note for CLARIFY-001..008 is absent on this branch.

findings.quoted_line: - **`leave_requests`** (UNCHANGED, referenced by name) — already carries `status`, `approver_id`, `cancelled_by`, `cancelled_at`, `reverses_request_id`. New indexes: standalone `status` (the existing `(employee_id, status)` cannot serve a status-only predicate — this is the first status-only access path in the codebase) and `approver_id` (recipient resolution for a cancelled APPROVED request). The queue query MUST also exclude `reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`: a cancelled-after-approval request is TWO rows, so without that predicate the reversal row is a spurious second queue entry. **NOT delivered as of Phase 1** — the delivered migration adds no `leave_requests` DDL at all; see *Phase 1 delivered* below.
